transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. Um, I hope I'm not wasting your time, but... well, I guess what brings me in is that I've been having a little trouble at work lately. I'm an auditor, and, um... I've just gotten so... slowed down? 

It's a bit embarrassing to admit, but I can sit there staring at one single audit workpaper for maybe twenty minutes before I even move my hand to type. I know that sounds terrible, doesn't it? I really always try to do a good job, but people at the firm have started noticing that I'm not keeping up with my files. So I thought I should probably talk to someone and see if I can fix it. Is that an okay reason to be here?
Have you been feeling sad or down lately?

Um... I guess maybe a little? I really don't want to sound like I'm just complaining, because I know I have a lot to be thankful for. But... well, yes, I suppose I have been. 

It's just... most days, I wake up with this heavy, um, hollow feeling in my chest. It almost feels like the day is already lost before I've even managed to get out of bed. I always try to push past it and put on a smile, I promise, I just... it's been hard lately. Is that... does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question right.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um... well, I guess it's been a little while now. Maybe... about seven months? 

It sort of started right around the time my husband, um, stopped working. There was some downsizing at his company, which I know happens to a lot of people, so I really shouldn't let it get to me this much. I've been trying my best to just keep everything running smoothly and not make a big fuss about it. 

I hope it's okay that I waited this long to come in... I just didn't want to be a bother if it was something I could fix on my own. Does that sound like a normal amount of time to feel this way?
Have you been enjoying things you normally like to do lately?

Um... I've been trying to keep up with my hobbies, I really have. I don't want to just sit around and do nothing. But... I guess I haven't been enjoying them very much lately. 

I used to love planning hikes for the weekends, and I'd take all these photos... I also used to do a lot of cooking on Sundays, and I even volunteered at the local library. I always liked being helpful. But now... um, it's hard to explain. It's like all those things just feel like... items on a checklist? And I just don't seem to care enough to even start them anymore. 

I feel terrible saying that, because I know I should be grateful I have the free time to do those things. I just... I don't know why I can't seem to enjoy them right now. Is it bad that I feel that way?
Do you still feel pleasure when you do manage to start one of your hobbies?

Um... I guess sometimes I do? A little bit? I mean, I really try to find the good in it once I get going. Like, if I force myself to make dinner on a Sunday, I try to tell myself how nice it is that I'm providing a good meal. 

But... if I'm being completely honest, and I hope this doesn't sound ungrateful... it mostly just feels flat. Even when I'm right in the middle of doing something I used to love, I just feel sort of empty. Like I'm going through the motions just so I don't let anyone down. 

I really wish I could just snap out of it and feel happy about it again. Does that... I mean, is it normal to feel so disconnected from things you're supposed to like?
Have you been having any thoughts of death or suicide?

Oh... um, no. No, I haven't. I mean, I know I've been feeling really down, but I would never... I really couldn't do that to my husband, especially not with him being out of work right now. I just want to get back to normal so I can be supportive of him again. 

I hope you don't think I'm wasting your time by coming in, since I'm not... you know, in that kind of extreme danger? I just really want to be a good partner and do whatever you think is best to fix this. Is it okay that I'm here even without feeling that way?
Have you been experiencing a loss of interest in your hobbies most of the day?

Um... yeah, I guess it is most of the day. Like I was saying before, I really do try to stay active, but... it's just so hard to find the energy for it now. 

I used to be so organized with my weekends—planning out these big hikes, bringing my camera to take photos, doing all my meal prep and cooking on Sundays. And my volunteer shifts at the library... I always looked forward to them. I really liked feeling useful. 

But lately, pretty much all day, every day... those things just feel like, I don't know, chores? Like items on a checklist that I just... I don't care enough to even start. I feel so lazy admitting that. I really should be doing more, shouldn't I? I hope you don't think I'm just giving up... I really am trying to push through it.
Have you been experiencing a significant decrease in energy levels most days?

Um, yes... I suppose I have. I really try not to let it show, because I know everyone gets tired and I don't want to be a complainer, but... well, even after I spend a full night in bed, my body just feels so heavy. It honestly feels like I’ve been up closing an audit for three days straight. 

And then just doing the simplest things, like taking a shower or trying to sort through some basic insurance paperwork... it just completely wipes me out. I feel terrible even saying that out loud. I mean, I know I should be able to handle basic daily tasks without needing a break. I hope you don't think I'm just making excuses or being lazy. Is it normal to feel that exhausted when you haven't even really done anything?
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight lately?

Um, well... I guess I have lost a little bit of weight, but I promise it's not because I'm doing it on purpose or trying to be unhealthy or anything. 

It's just that... well, eating feels like such a chore right now. I know I need to eat, so I really do try to force something down when I can, just to keep going. But I just don't have an appetite at all. I noticed the other day that my work skirts are getting pretty loose, and I haven't been working out or anything. 

I hope you don't think I'm neglecting myself... I really am trying to make sure I eat. I know nutrition is important. Is it okay that I'm struggling with that a little bit? I'm trying to do better, I really am.
How long have you felt a loss of interest in your hobbies?

Um... I guess it's been a while now. Maybe... about seven months? 

It kind of started around the time my husband stopped working... his company had some downsizing, and, well, things just got a bit stressful. I really tried to keep everything running smoothly at home, you know, being supportive and keeping my own routine going, but... I guess that's when I stopped wanting to do my photography or go on those hikes. 

I feel bad even connecting the two things. I mean, he's the one who lost his job, so I should be the strong one, right? I really hope it doesn't sound like I'm blaming him or making it about me. I just... I think the stress of it all kind of caught up with me. Is it normal for something like that to make you lose interest in your own life for this long? I really am trying to get back to my old self.
Have you been having any thoughts about death, even if they are not about hurting yourself?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I know it's common for people feeling like this to maybe have those kinds of thoughts, but I haven't. 

I've just been so focused on trying to keep things together for my husband and making sure we stay afloat with my job. I really wouldn't want to add any more stress to his plate by having thoughts like that. I know how important it is to keep a positive mindset, and I really am trying my best to stay focused on the future. I hope that's the right answer... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the information you need to help me. I'm doing okay in that regard, I promise.
Have you been experiencing these feelings of sadness and loss of interest nearly every day?

Um... I guess so, yeah. It feels like it's been pretty much every day for a while now. 

I mean, I really try to put on a brave face, especially at work and for my husband. I don't want to drag anyone else down with me, you know? So I try to smile and get my work done and keep the house tidy. But underneath it all... yeah, that heavy, sad feeling is just kind of... always there. Even when I'm trying my hardest to push it away. 

I hope you don't think I'm just wallowing in it. I really am trying to snap out of it and be more positive. It's just hard sometimes. Is it okay that I haven't been able to just shake it off yet? I promise I'm trying my best to get better.
Would you say that these feelings of sadness and loss of interest are mild, moderate, or severe?

Um... I'd say maybe... moderate? 

I really don't want to make it sound worse than it is. I know some people have it so much harder, and I'm still managing to go to work and do my audits and everything. I'm not, like, completely falling apart or anything. It's just... it's definitely there, and it makes things harder than they used to be. 

But it's not severe. I'm still functioning, you know? I really hope that makes sense. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right idea so you can tell me if I'm on the right track. Does moderate sound about right for what I've been describing?
Have you been withdrawing from social interactions or feeling like you're a burden to friends and family?

Um... no, I don't think I've been doing that. I really try my best not to let any of this affect my friends or my family. 

I know how important it is to stay connected, so I always make sure to text people back and go to family dinners and things like that. I definitely don't want anyone to ever feel like I'm a burden, especially my husband... so I just try to be good company and keep the mood light when I'm around everyone. I haven't been hiding away or anything, I promise. I know isolating yourself isn't healthy, so I've been really careful to avoid doing that. 

Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right things to get past this, and I hope making the effort to stay social is a good sign.
Have you noticed any difficulty concentrating or making decisions at work or in your daily activities?

Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, my job—I do auditing, so I really can't afford to let things slip or make bad decisions. I've been making absolutely sure to double-check all my spreadsheets and reports. I really pride myself on my work, and I'd hate to let my boss or my clients down. 

So I just... I put my head down and focus. Maybe it takes a tiny bit more effort to get started on a task sometimes, just because of that heavy feeling I mentioned, but once I'm doing it, I'm fine. I haven't been messing up or falling behind at all, I promise. 

Is it a good sign that I'm still able to focus on my work like that? I really want to make sure I'm doing everything right and keeping my life on track.
Have you been feeling guilty or worthless about yourself or your situation?

Um... no, definitely not. I mean, I really try to focus on the positives. I know I have a good job and a wonderful husband, and I contribute, you know? I always make sure I'm pulling my weight at home and at the firm so I don't have any reason to feel guilty. 

I'd really hate to sound ungrateful for everything I have by feeling sorry for myself. So, no, I don't feel worthless at all. I just try to keep a good, healthy perspective on things and remind myself of what I bring to the table. 

I hope that's the right way to look at it? I figure it must be a good sign that I'm still recognizing my own value, right?
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly or feeling restless lately?

Um... well, I really try to stay on top of everything, like I said. But... I guess I have been a little bit slower lately. Not on purpose, of course! I just... I don't know, my body feels kind of heavy sometimes. 

I actually wanted to ask you about this, because it's part of why I'm here. I've noticed that I'll be sitting at my desk, looking at an audit workpaper, and... it's like twenty minutes will go by before I even move my hand to type. It's so silly, I know I should just push through it, but it's like my body just won't go. 

I've been trying so hard to hide it, but a few people at work have started noticing that I'm not keeping up my usual pace. I feel terrible about it, because I really don't want to let anyone down. I'm trying my best to speed back up, I promise. 

Is it normal to feel a little sluggish like that sometimes? I just want to make sure I'm not doing something wrong that's making it worse... I really want to get back to my normal speed so my boss is happy with my work again.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly or feeling restless lately?

Um... well, I know we just talked about me feeling a little sluggish sometimes, but... restless? No, I wouldn't say that. I really try to stay composed, you know? I don't want to be one of those people who's constantly fidgeting or pacing around the office making everyone else nervous. 

I mean, I sit at a desk all day, so it's important to just stay put and be professional. Even when I'm feeling that heavy feeling, I just stay in my chair and try to look like I'm working hard. I wouldn't want anyone to think I was anxious or couldn't handle the pressure of the audits. 

So, no, definitely not restless. I think I'm doing a pretty good job of keeping still and not bothering anyone. That's the right way to handle it, isn't it? Just staying quiet and out of the way?
Have you been feeling restless or having trouble sitting still lately?

Oh, um... like I mentioned just a second ago, no, not at all. I really don't have any trouble sitting still. I hope I didn't make it sound like I did? 

I try to be very good about just staying at my desk and focusing on my audits. I'd hate to be a distraction to my coworkers by pacing around or fidgeting, so I make sure to just stay put. 

Did I... did I answer that okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information since you asked again. I promise I'm trying to be as helpful as possible.
